data: Create an original dark Guernica-like cubist mural as a compressed horizontal frieze filling the entire image, replacing the gallery wall and all its framed artworks with one shallow, fractured painted field. Use the first image only as compositional context for the broad horizontal arrangement and collective gallery-display logic, while rendering no gallery architecture. Build the mural from large interlocking black, ash-gray, and stained-ivory planes with sharp charcoal contours, rough oil scumbling, scraped edges, and scratched plaster. Distort every human into a blunt mask with mismatched, displaced eyes, noses, and mouths; reduce bodies, hands, garments, and objects to flat angular signs and broken silhouettes. At the center, surround a strong abstract shield representing firewalls and protection. Multiple figures cluster around it, their angular arms and hands reaching inward to reinforce, brace, and stabilize its fractured perimeter. Integrate the woman from the second image as the central guiding figure, fully reimagined as the Woman with Lamp: preserve her profile silhouette and lamp motif but transform her into a stained-ivory cubist face and angular body, holding a stark ivory lamp that directs the repair. Her gesture aligns the shield’s displaced planes into ordered sections. Keep the near-monochrome palette, with no saturated color, photographic detail, natural anatomy, realistic perspective, or dimensional staging. Use steady frontal illumination and hard-edged painted shadows within the frieze to emphasize cooperation, control, and the motif of Member state unity under stress.
